summary.para: Creates a read-write IList<T> wrapper around an array. When an array is implicitely converted to an IList<T>, changes to the items in the array cannot be made through the interface. This method creates a read-write IList<T> wrapper on an array that can be used to make changes to the array.

Use this method when you need to pass an array to an algorithms that takes an IList<T> and that tries to modify items in the list. Algorithms in this class generally do not need this method, since they have been design to operate on arrays even when they are passed as an IList<T>.

member.remarks: Since arrays cannot be resized, inserting an item causes the last item in the array to be automatically removed. Removing an item causes the last item in the array to be replaced with a default value (0 or null). Clearing the list causes all the items to be replaced with a default value.
member.param: The array to wrap.
member.returns: An IList<T> wrapper onto .

member.name: M:Halfling.Collections.Algorithms.GeneratePermutations``1(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{``0})
member.summary: Generates all the possible permutations of the items in . If has N items, then N factorial permutations will be generated. This method does not compare the items to determine if any of them are equal. If some items are equal, the same permutation may be generated more than once. For example, if the collections contains the three items A, A, and B, then this method will generate the six permutations, AAB, AAB, ABA, ABA, BAA, BAA (not necessarily in that order). To take equal items into account, use the GenerateSortedPermutations method.
member.typeparam: The type of items to permute.
member.param: The collection of items to permute.
member.returns: An IEnumerable<T[]> that enumerations all the possible permutations of the items in . Each permutations is returned as an array. The items in the array should be copied if they need to be used after the next permutation is generated; each permutation may reuse the same array instance.

member.summary: Performs a lexicographical comparison of two sequences of values. A lexicographical comparison compares corresponding pairs of elements from two sequences in order. If the first element of sequence1 is less than the first element of sequence2, then the comparison ends and the first sequence is lexicographically less than the second. If the first elements of each sequence are equal, then the comparison proceeds to the second element of each sequence. If one sequence is shorter than the other, but corresponding elements are all equal, then the shorter sequence is considered less than the longer one.
member.remarks: T must implement either IComparable<T> and this implementation is used to compare the items.
member.typeparam: Types of items to compare. This type must implement IComparable<T> to allow items to be compared.
member.param: The first sequence to compare.
The second sequence to compare.
member.returns: Less than zero if is lexicographically less than . Greater than zero if is lexicographically greater than . Zero if is equal to .
member.exception: T does not implement IComparable<T> or IComparable.

member.name: T:Halfling.Collections.Bag`1
member.summary: Bag<T> is a collection that contains items of type T. Unlike a Set, duplicate items (items that compare equal to each other) are allowed in an Bag.

remarks.p: The items are compared in one of two ways. If T implements IComparable<T> then the Equals method of that interface will be used to compare items, otherwise the Equals method from Object will be used. Alternatively, an instance of IComparer<T> can be passed to the constructor to use to compare items.
Bag is implemented as a hash table. Inserting, deleting, and looking up an an element all are done in approximately constant time, regardless of the number of items in the bag.

When multiple equal items are stored in the bag, they are stored as a representative item and a count. If equal items can be distinguished, this may be noticable. For example, if a case-insensitive comparer is used with a Bag<string>, and both "hello", and "HELLO" are added to the bag, then the bag will appear to contain two copies of "hello" (the representative item).
is similar, but uses comparison instead of hashing, maintain the items in sorted order, and stores distinct copies of items that compare equal.

member.name: M:Halfling.Collections.Bag`1.GetEnumerator
member.summary: Returns an enumerator that enumerates all the items in the bag. If an item is present multiple times in the bag, the representative item is yielded by the enumerator multiple times. The order of enumeration is haphazard and may change.

remarks.p: Typically, this method is not called directly. Instead the "foreach" statement is used to enumerate the items, which uses this method implicitly.

member.name: T:Halfling.Collections.BigList`1
member.summary: BigList<T> provides a list of items, in order, with indices of the items ranging from 0 to one less than the count of items in the collection. BigList<T> is optimized for efficient operations on large (>100 items) lists, especially for insertions, deletions, copies, and concatinations.

remarks.para: BigList<T> class is similar in functionality to the standard List<T> class. Both classes provide a collection that stores an set of items in order, with indices of the items ranging from 0 to one less than the count of items in the collection. Both classes provide the ability to add and remove items from any index, and the get or set the item at any index.

BigList<T> differs significantly from List<T> in the performance of various operations, especially when the lists become large (several hundred items or more). With List<T>, inserting or removing elements from anywhere in a large list except the end is very inefficient -- every item after the point of inserting or deletion has to be moved in the list. The BigList<T> class, however, allows for fast insertions and deletions anywhere in the list. Furthermore, BigList<T> allows copies of a list, sub-parts of a list, and concatinations of two lists to be very fast. When a copy is made of part or all of a BigList, two lists shared storage for the parts of the lists that are the same. Only when one of the lists is changed is additional memory allocated to store the distinct parts of the lists.

Of course, there is a small price to pay for this extra flexibility. Although still quite efficient, using an index to get or change one element of a BigList, while still reasonably efficient, is significantly slower than using a plain List. Because of this, if you want to process every element of a BigList, using a foreach loop is a lot more efficient than using a for loop and indexing the list.

In general, use a List when the only operations you are using are Add (to the end), foreach, or indexing, or you are very sure the list will always remain small (less than 100 items). For large (>100 items) lists that do insertions, removals, copies, concatinations, or sub-ranges, BigList will be more efficient than List. In almost all cases, BigList is more efficient and easier to use than LinkedList.

member.typeparam: The type of items to store in the BigList.

member.name: M:Halfling.Collections.BigList`1.Range(System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Returns a view onto a sub-range of this list. Items are not copied; the returned IList<T> is simply a different view onto the same underlying items. Changes to this list are reflected in the view, and vice versa. Insertions and deletions in the view change the size of the view, but insertions and deletions in the underlying list do not.
member.remarks:
If a copy of the sub-range is desired, use the method instead.
This method can be used to apply an algorithm to a portion of a list. For example: Algorithms.ReverseInPlace(list.Range(3, 6)) will reverse the 6 items beginning at index 3.
member.param: The starting index of the view.

member.name: T:Halfling.Collections.Deque`1

summary.para: The Deque class implements a type of list known as a Double Ended Queue. A Deque is quite similar to a List, in that items have indices (starting at 0), and the item at any index can be efficiently retrieved. The difference between a List and a Deque lies in the efficiency of inserting elements at the beginning. In a List, items can be efficiently added to the end, but inserting an item at the beginning of the List is slow, taking time proportional to the size of the List. In a Deque, items can be added to the beginning or end equally efficiently, regardless of the number of items in the Deque. As a trade-off for this increased flexibility, Deque is somewhat slower than List (but still constant time) when being indexed to get or retrieve elements.

remarks.para: The Deque class can also be used as a more flexible alternative to the Queue and Stack classes. Deque is as efficient as Queue and Stack for adding or removing items, but is more flexible: it allows access to all items in the queue, and allows adding or removing from either end.
Deque is implemented as a ring buffer, which is grown as necessary. The size of the buffer is doubled whenever the existing capacity is too small to hold all the elements.

member.typeparam: The type of items stored in the Deque.

member.summary: Gets or sets the capacity of the Deque. The Capacity is the number of items that this Deque can hold without expanding its internal buffer. Since Deque will automatically expand its buffer when necessary, in almost all cases it is unnecessary to worry about the capacity. However, if it is known that a Deque will contain exactly 1000 items eventually, it can slightly improve efficiency to set the capacity to 1000 up front, so that the Deque does not have to expand automatically.

member.summary: Returns a view onto a sub-range of this list. Items are not copied; the returned IList<T> is simply a different view onto the same underlying items. summary.para: The MultiDictionary class that associates values with a key. Unlike an Dictionary, each key can have multiple values associated with it. When indexing an MultiDictionary, instead of a single value associated with a key, you retrieve an enumeration of values.
When constructed, you can chose to allow the same value to be associated with a key multiple times, or only one time.

member.name: M:Halfling.Collections.MultiDictionary`2.#ctor(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Create a new MultiDictionary. The default ordering of keys and values are used. If duplicate values are allowed, multiple copies of the same value can be associated with the same key. For example, the key "foo" could have "a", "a", and "b" associated with it. If duplicate values are not allowed, only one copies of a given value can be associated with the same key, although different keys can have the same value. For example, the key "foo" could have "a" and "b" associated with it, which key "bar" has values "b" and "c" associated with it.
member.remarks: The default ordering of keys and values will be used, as defined by TKey and TValue's implementation of IComparable<T> (or IComparable if IComparable<T> is not implemented). If a different ordering should be used, other constructors allow a custom Comparer or IComparer to be passed to changed the ordering.
member.param: Can the same value be associated with a key multiple times?
member.exception: TKey or TValue does not implement either IComparable<T> or IComparable.

member.name: T:Halfling.Collections.MultiDictionaryBase`2
member.summary: MultiDictionaryBase is a base class that can be used to more easily implement a class that associates multiple values to a single key. The class implements the generic IDictionary<TKey, ICollection<TValue>> interface.

remarks.para: To use MultiDictionaryBase as a base class, the derived class must override Count, Clear, Add, Remove(TKey), Remove(TKey,TValue), Contains(TKey,TValue), EnumerateKeys, and TryEnumerateValuesForKey.
It may wish consider overriding CountValues, CountAllValues, ContainsKey, and EqualValues, but these are not required.

member.name: T:Halfling.Collections.OrderedBag`1
member.summary: OrderedBag<T> is a collection that contains items of type T. The item are maintained in a sorted order. Unlike a OrderedSet, duplicate items (items that compare equal to each other) are allows in an OrderedBag.

remarks.p: The items are compared in one of three ways. If T implements IComparable<TKey> or IComparable, then the CompareTo method of that interface will be used to compare items. Alternatively, a comparison function can be passed in either as a delegate, or as an instance of IComparer<TKey>.

OrderedBag is implemented as a balanced binary tree. Inserting, deleting, and looking up an an element all are done in log(N) + M time, where N is the number of keys in the tree, and M is the current number of copies of the element being handled.
is similar, but uses hashing instead of comparison, and does not maintain the keys in sorted order.

member.name: T:Halfling.Collections.OrderedDictionary`2
member.summary: OrderedDictionary<TKey, TValue> is a collection that maps keys of type TKey to values of type TValue. The keys are maintained in a sorted order, and at most one value is permitted for each key.

remarks.p: The keys are compared in one of three ways. If TKey implements IComparable<TKey> or IComparable, then the CompareTo method of that interface will be used to compare elements. Alternatively, a comparison function can be passed in either as a delegate, or as an instance of IComparer<TKey>.
OrderedDictionary is implemented as a balanced binary tree. Inserting, deleting, and looking up an an element all are done in log(N) type, where N is the number of keys in the tree.
is similar, but uses hashing instead of comparison, and does not maintain the keys in sorted order.

member.name: M:Halfling.Collections.OrderedMultiDictionary`2.#ctor(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Create a new OrderedMultiDictionary. The default ordering of keys and values are used. If duplicate values are allowed, multiple copies of the same value can be associated with the same key. For example, the key "foo" could have "a", "a", and "b" associated with it. If duplicate values are not allowed, only one copies of a given value can be associated with the same key, although different keys can have the same value. For example, the key "foo" could have "a" and "b" associated with it, which key "bar" has values "b" and "c" associated with it.
member.remarks: The default ordering of keys and values will be used, as defined by TKey and TValue's implementation of IComparable<T> (or IComparable if IComparable<T> is not implemented). If a different ordering should be used, other constructors allow a custom Comparer or IComparer to be passed to changed the ordering.
member.param: Can the same value be associated with a key multiple times?
member.exception: TKey or TValue does not implement either IComparable<T> or IComparable.

member.name: T:Halfling.Collections.OrderedSet`1
member.summary: OrderedSet<T> is a collection that contains items of type T. The item are maintained in a sorted order, and duplicate items are not allowed. Each item has an index in the set: the smallest item has index 0, the next smallest item has index 1, and so forth.

remarks.p: The items are compared in one of three ways. If T implements IComparable<TKey> or IComparable, then the CompareTo method of that interface will be used to compare items. Alternatively, a comparison function can be passed in either as a delegate, or as an instance of IComparer<TKey>.
OrderedSet is implemented as a balanced binary tree. Inserting, deleting, and looking up an an element all are done in log(N) type, where N is the number of keys in the tree.

member.name: T:Halfling.Collections.OrderedSet`1.View
member.summary: The OrderedSet<T>.View class is used to look at a subset of the Items inside an ordered set. It is returned from the Range, RangeTo, RangeFrom, and Reversed methods.

member.name: M:Halfling.Geometry.Ray.EaseOut(Halfling.Geometry.Ray@,Halfling.Geometry.Ray@,System.Single)
member.summary: Returns 'from' interpolated towards 'to' by 't'. The 't' field will be clamped to the range [0,1]. If 't' is 0, returns 'from'. If 't' is 1, returns 'to'. The returned value will be "eased out" such that it increases more slowly as 't' increases.

member.name: M:Halfling.Geometry.Ray.EaseInOut(Halfling.Geometry.Ray@,Halfling.Geometry.Ray@,System.Single)
member.summary: Returns 'from' interpolated towards 'to' by 't'. The 't' field will be clamped to the range [0,1]. If 't' is 0, returns 'from'. If 't' is 1, returns 'to'. The returned value will be "eased in and out" such that it increases slowly when t is near 0 or near 1.

member.name: M:Halfling.Geometry.Rect.Lerp(Halfling.Geometry.Rect@,Halfling.Geometry.Rect@,System.Single)
member.summary: Returns 'from' linearly interpolated towards 'to' by 't'. The 't' field will be clamped to the range [0,1]. If 't' is 0, returns 'from'. If 't' is 1, returns 'to'. If 't' is .5, returns the average of 'from' and 'to'.

member.name: M:Halfling.Geometry.Rect.EaseIn(Halfling.Geometry.Rect@,Halfling.Geometry.Rect@,System.Single)
member.summary: Returns 'from' interpolated towards 'to' by 't'. The 't' field will be clamped to the range [0,1]. If 't' is 0, returns 'from'. If 't' is 1, returns 'to'. The returned value will be "eased in" such that it increases more quickly as 't' increases.

member.name: M:Halfling.Geometry.Rect.EaseOut(Halfling.Geometry.Rect@,Halfling.Geometry.Rect@,System.Single)
member.summary: Returns 'from' interpolated towards 'to' by 't'. The 't' field will be clamped to the range [0,1]. If 't' is 0, returns 'from'. If 't' is 1, returns 'to'. The returned value will be "eased out" such that it increases more slowly as 't' increases.

member.name: M:Halfling.Geometry.Rect.EaseInOut(Halfling.Geometry.Rect@,Halfling.Geometry.Rect@,System.Single)
member.summary: Returns 'from' interpolated towards 'to' by 't'. The 't' field will be clamped to the range [0,1]. If 't' is 0, returns 'from'. If 't' is 1, returns 'to'. The returned value will be "eased in and out" such that it increases slowly when t is near 0 or near 1.

member.name: M:Halfling.Geometry.Segment.Lerp(Halfling.Geometry.Segment@,Halfling.Geometry.Segment@,System.Single)
member.summary: Returns 'from' linearly interpolated towards 'to' by 't'. The 't' field will be clamped to the range [0,1]. If 't' is 0, returns 'from'. If 't' is 1, returns 'to'. If 't' is .5, returns the average of 'from' and 'to'.

member.name: M:Halfling.Geometry.Segment.EaseIn(Halfling.Geometry.Segment@,Halfling.Geometry.Segment@,System.Single)
member.summary: Returns 'from' interpolated towards 'to' by 't'. The 't' field will be clamped to the range [0,1]. If 't' is 0, returns 'from'. If 't' is 1, returns 'to'. The returned value will be "eased in" such that it increases more quickly as 't' increases.

member.name: M:Halfling.Geometry.Segment.EaseOut(Halfling.Geometry.Segment@,Halfling.Geometry.Segment@,System.Single)
member.summary: Returns 'from' interpolated towards 'to' by 't'. The 't' field will be clamped to the range [0,1]. If 't' is 0, returns 'from'. If 't' is 1, returns 'to'. The returned value will be "eased out" such that it increases more slowly as 't' increases.

member.name: M:Halfling.Geometry.Segment.EaseInOut(Halfling.Geometry.Segment@,Halfling.Geometry.Segment@,System.Single)
member.summary: Returns 'from' interpolated towards 'to' by 't'. The 't' field will be clamped to the range [0,1]. If 't' is 0, returns 'from'. If 't' is 1, returns 'to'. The returned value will be "eased in and out" such that it increases slowly when t is near 0 or near 1.

member.name: T:Halfling.Geometry.VHex
member.summary: Stores the coordinates of a particular flat-topped hex on a "vertical" hex grid using an "axial" coordinate system. A 3rd implicit Z coordinate is automatically computed for use in algorithms that require a "cube" coordinate system.
member.remarks: The coordinate system used and most of the hex algorithms in this class are taken from http://www.redblobgames.com/grids/hexagons/

member.name: P:Halfling.Graphics.GraphicsManager.BaseTransform
member.summary: Gets the transform at the top of the transform stack, or the identity matrix if the transform stack is empty.

member.name: P:Halfling.Graphics.GraphicsManager.Viewport
member.summary: Gets or sets the pixel rectangle on the current RenderTarget (or the window if RenderTarget is null) onto which graphics will be rendered. Post-transformation coordinates in the range (-1,-1)->(1,1) will be mapped to this rect. If null, the entire current render target will be used. By convention the value of this property must be restored after changing.

member.name: P:Halfling.Graphics.GraphicsManager.Clipper
member.summary: Gets or sets a pixel rectangle (relative to the top-left of the current Viewport, if any) outside of which no pixels will be rendered. By convention the value of this property must be restored after changing.

member.name: P:Halfling.Graphics.GraphicsManager.BaseClipper
member.summary: Gets the clipper at the top of the clipper stack, or null if the clipper stack is empty.

member.name: P:Halfling.Graphics.GraphicsManager.RenderTarget
member.summary: Gets or sets the RenderTarget texture onto which graphics will be rendered. If null, graphics will be rendered directly onto the window. By convention the value of this property must be restored after changing.

member.name: P:Halfling.Graphics.GraphicsManager.BaseRenderTarget
member.summary: Gets the RenderTarget at the top of the render target stack, or null if the render target stack is empty.

member.name: P:Halfling.Graphics.GraphicsManager.TargetBlendMode
member.summary: Gets or sets how rendered pixels will be combined with existing pixels (on the current RenderTarget, or the window if the RenderTarget is null). By convention the value of this property does not need to be restored after changing.

member.name: P:Halfling.Graphics.GraphicsManager.DepthBufferMode
member.summary: Gets or sets the behavior of the depth buffer of the current RenderTarget (or of the window if RenderTarget is null). The depth buffer is disabled by default. By convention the value of this property must be restored after changing.

member.name: P:Halfling.Graphics.GraphicsManager.StencilBufferMode
member.summary: Gets or sets the behavior of the stencil buffer of the current RenderTarget (or of the window if RenderTarget is null). The stencil buffer is disabled by default. By convention the value of this property must be restored after changing.

member.name: P:Halfling.Graphics.GraphicsManager.ChannelWriteMask
member.summary: Gets or sets a set of flags indicating which color channels will be written during rendering. The default is all channels. By convention the value of this property must be restored after changing.

member.name: P:Halfling.Graphics.GraphicsManager.Textures
member.summary: Gets the component that creates and loads textures.

member.name: P:Halfling.Graphics.GraphicsManager.Shaders
member.summary: Gets the component that creates and loads vertex and pixel shaders.

member.name: P:Halfling.Graphics.GraphicsManager.Fonts
member.summary: Gets the component that creates and loads fonts.

member.name: P:Halfling.Graphics.GraphicsManager.Capabilities

member.name: M:Halfling.Graphics.GraphicsManager.DrawInterleaved``2(Halfling.Graphics.GraphicsArray{``0},Halfling.Graphics.GraphicsArray{``1},System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Draws the specified range of primitives in the specified interleaved GraphicsArrays to the current RenderTarget, or directly to the window if RenderTarget is null. Each GraphicsArray should store different, complementary types of primitive whose vertex data will be interleaved together on the GPU to create the final vertexes. The primitive types must have the same underlying type, number of underlying primitives, and index pattern.

member.name: M:Halfling.Graphics.GraphicsManager.Clear
member.summary: Clears the color, depth, and stencil buffers of the current RenderTarget (or the window if RenderTarget is null) to black, 1.0, and 0, respectively. If a Viewport is set, only those pixels inside the current Viewport rectangle will be cleared. If a Clipper is set, only those pixels inside the current Clipper rectangle will be cleared.

member.name: M:Halfling.Graphics.GraphicsManager.Clear(System.Nullable{Halfling.Graphics.Color},System.Nullable{System.Single},System.Nullable{System.Byte})
member.summary: Clears the color, depth, and/or stencil buffers of the current RenderTarget (or the window if RenderTarget is null). If a Viewport is set, only those pixels inside the current Viewport rectangle will be cleared. If a Clipper is set, only those pixels inside the current Clipper rectangle will be cleared.
member.param: The color to which the pixels in the depth buffer should be set, or null to not clear the color buffer.
The value to which the pixels in the depth buffer should be set, or null to not clear the depth buffer. Typically, this is 1.0f.
The value to which the pixels in the stencil buffer should be set, or null to not clear the stencil buffer. Typically, this is 0.

member.name: M:Halfling.Graphics.GraphicsManager.PushTransform
member.summary: Pushes the current Transform matrix onto the transform stack so that it can be restored by calling PopTransform(). Does not actually modify the current transform.
member.returns: An object that when disposed (i.e., within a 'using' block) will call PopTransform().

member.returns: An object that when disposed (i.e., within a 'using' block) will call PopTransform().

member.name: M:Halfling.Graphics.GraphicsManager.PushTransformMultiply(Halfling.Geometry.Matrix)

member.returns: An object that when disposed (i.e., within a 'using' block) will call PopTransform().

member.name: M:Halfling.Graphics.GraphicsManager.PopTransform
member.summary: Pops the most-recently-pushed matrix off of the transform stack and restores the Transform property to that matrix.

member.name: P:Halfling.Graphics.RenderTrees.InternalNode.Clipper
member.summary: Gets or sets the pixel region outside of which pixels will not be rendered. If both a parent and a descendent specify a clipper, then the actual clipped region will be the intersection of the clippers.
member.remarks: This is typed as Rect instead of IntRect (even though GraphicsManager takes an IntRect clipper) because the clipper may get scaled and we want to be able to specify clippers that are (unscaled) sub-pixel in size.

member.name: T:Halfling.Graphics.TargetBlendMode
member.summary: Specifies how pixels in the color buffer are modified as additional pixels are rendered overtop.
member.remarks: Blending of the RGB color channels is defined by the equation: RgbOperator([sourceRGB] * SourceRgbFactor, [destRGB] * DestRgbFactor) Blending of the alpha channel is defined by the equation: AlphaOperator([sourceAlpha] * SourceAlphaFactor, [destAlpha] * DestAlphaFactor)

member.name: F:Halfling.Graphics.TargetBlendMode.AlphaBlend
member.summary: The source pixel will be interpolated onto the existing destination pixel using the source pixel's alpha value.

member.name: F:Halfling.Graphics.TargetBlendMode.AlphaBlendPreMultiplied
member.summary: The source pixel will be interpolated onto the existing destination pixel using the source pixel's alpha value, except that it is assumed that the source pixel's RGB channels will already have been multiplied by its alpha channel by the pixel shader.

member.name: F:Halfling.Graphics.TargetBlendMode.ReplaceNoBlend
member.summary: The destination pixel will be set to equal the source pixel, regardless of the existing destination pixel.

member.name: F:Halfling.Graphics.TargetBlendMode.Add
member.summary: The color and alpha channels of the source pixel will be added to those of the the existing destination pixel.

member.name: F:Halfling.Graphics.TargetBlendMode.AddAlphaBlend
member.summary: The color and alpha channels of the source pixel will be added to those of the the existing destination pixel.

member.name: F:Halfling.Graphics.TargetBlendMode.SubtractSourceFromDest
member.summary: The color and alpha channels of the source pixel will be subtracted from those of the existing destination pixel.

member.name: F:Halfling.Graphics.TargetBlendMode.SubtractDestFromSource
member.summary: The color and alpha channels of the existing destination pixel will be subtracted from those of the source pixel.

member.name: F:Halfling.Graphics.TargetBlendMode.Multiply
member.summary: The color and alpha channels of the source pixel will be multiplied with those of the destination pixel.

member.name: F:Halfling.Graphics.TargetBlendMode.Min
member.summary: The color and alpha channels of the destination pixel will be individually set to the lesser of those of the source and existing destination pixels.

member.name: F:Halfling.Graphics.TargetBlendMode.Max
member.summary: The color and alpha channels of the destination pixel will be individually set to the greater of those of the source and existing destination pixels.

member.name: F:Halfling.Graphics.BlendFactor.Zero
member.summary: The color or alpha value will be zeroed.

member.name: F:Halfling.Graphics.BlendFactor.One
member.summary: The color or alpha value will be sent to the BlendOperator unchanged.

member.name: F:Halfling.Graphics.BlendFactor.SourceColor

member.name: F:Halfling.Graphics.BlendFactor.SourceAlpha

member.name: F:Halfling.Graphics.BlendFactor.InverseSourceAlpha

member.name: F:Halfling.Graphics.BlendFactor.DestColor
member.summary: Each channel of the RGB color value will be multiplied with the corresponding color channel of the existing destination color. This flag cannot be used with SourceAlphaFactor or DestAlphaFactor.

member.name: F:Halfling.Graphics.BlendFactor.InverseDestColor
member.summary: Each channel of the RGB color value will be multiplied with the inverse of the corresponding color channel of the existing destination color. The inverse is defined as 1 minus the normalized (0-1) channel value. This flag cannot be used with SourceAlphaFactor or DestAlphaFactor.

member.name: F:Halfling.Graphics.BlendFactor.DestAlpha

member.name: F:Halfling.Graphics.BlendFactor.InverseDestAlpha
member.summary: Each channel of the RGB color or alpha value will be multiplied with the inverse of the alpha value of the existing destination color. The inverse is defined as 1 minus the normalized (0-1) channel value.

member.summary: Specifies the format to use when compressing a texture.

member.name: F:Halfling.Graphics.CompressionFormat.None
member.summary: The texture will not be compressed.

member.name: F:Halfling.Graphics.CompressionFormat.NoAlpha
member.summary: The texture will be compressed without an alpha channel. This generally uses BC1/DXT1 compression and is smaller than FullAlpha.

member.name: F:Halfling.Graphics.CompressionFormat.AlphaCutout
member.summary: The texture will be compressed with a 1-bit alpha channel. This generally uses BC1/DXT1 compression and is smaller than FullAlpha.

member.name: F:Halfling.Graphics.CompressionFormat.FullAlpha
member.summary: The texture will be compressed with a full alpha channel. This generally uses BC3/DXT5 compression and is larger than NoAlpha or AlphaCutout.

member.name: F:Halfling.Graphics.CompressionFormat.NormalMap
member.summary: The texture will be compressed as a normal map where the X value uses the alpha channel, the Y value uses the green channel, and the Z value is inferred from the X and Y values. This generally uses BC3/DXT5 compression.

member.name: P:Halfling.Gui.GuiRoot`1.UIScale
member.summary: Gets the number of pixels occupied by a single UI-relative distance unit. This will be equal to OverrideUIScale if that is not null, otherwise it will be equal to the static GlobalUIScale property.

member.name: P:Halfling.Gui.Widget.AnchorRect
member.summary: Gets or sets the rect in the parent to which this Widget is anchored. Use the AnchorPresets static class for a list of pre-defined anchor rects. This property will be copied by the CopySettingsFrom() method.
member.remarks:
The coordinates of the AnchorRect are normalized between 0 and 1. For example, an x value of 0.0 indicates the left-most edge of the parent, a value of 0.5 indicates the center of the parent, and a value of 1.0 indicates the right-most edge of the parent.
The coordinates of each Left, Right, Top, and Bottom edge of Rect are pixel-offsets from the corresponding edge of AnchorRect.

member.summary: Reads a variable-length unsigned 32-bit integer from this BinaryReader. If the value is less than 128, one byte will be used. If the value is greater than 127 but less than 16384, two bytes will be used. If the value is greater than 16383 but less than 2097152, three bytes will be used. member.name: M:Halfling.Mathx.MoveToward(System.Double,System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Returns the result of moving 'current' towards 'target' by 'delta'. The returned value will never move past 'target' even if 'delta' is greater than the difference of 'target' and 'current'. If 'delta' is negative, 'current' will move away from 'target'. If 'current' and 'target' are equal, then the value of 'delta' is irrelevant regardless of its sign.

member.name: P:Halfling.ObjectBits.OBNode.NodeType
member.summary: Gets the current type of data or children stored by this OBNode. To change the current type, use one of the ChangeTo*() methods.

member.name: P:Halfling.ObjectBits.OBNode.Data
member.summary: Gets or sets this OBNode's byte data array. Modifying the returned array will modify the stored data. Getting this property is only legal if this OBNode's type is Data. Setting this property is only legal if this OBNode's type is Data or Unset. Setting this property when its type is Unset will automatically change its type to Data.

member.name: P:Halfling.ObjectBits.OBNode.ChildCount
member.summary: Gets the number of children contained by this OBNode. This will always return 0 if this OBNode's type is not ChildList or ChildMap.

member.name: P:Halfling.ObjectBits.OBNode.Item(System.Int32)
member.summary: Gets or sets the child OBNode at the specified index. Getting or setting this property is only legal if this OBNode's type is ChildList. When setting this property, there must already be a child at the existing index to replace.

member.name: P:Halfling.ObjectBits.OBNode.Item(System.String)
member.summary: Gets or sets the child OBNode associated with the specified string key. Getting this property is only legal if this OBNode's type is ChildMap. Setting this property is only legal if this OBNode's type if ChildMap or Unset. Setting this property when its type is Unset will automatically change its type to ChildMap.

member.name: P:Halfling.ObjectBits.OBNode.LinkTarget
member.summary: Gets or sets the node to which this OBNode is linked, or null if it is not linked to a node. Getting this property is only legal if this OBNode's type is Link. Setting this property is only legal if this OBNode's type is Link or Unset. Setting this property when its type is Unset will automatically change its type to Link.

member.name: P:Halfling.ObjectBits.OBNode.FinalLinkTarget
member.summary: Gets the final non-Link node in the linked node chain starting with this node. If the final link node in the chain links is null, returns null. If this node is not a Link node, simply returns this node. This method will *not* detect circular references; any circular references in the link chain will cause an infinite loop.

member.name: T:Halfling.Performance.FastClear2DArray`1
member.summary: Stores a rectangular, 2-dimensional array of elements. This class is faster than using a regular 2D array, because it uses a 1D array internally. Note that, unlike regular arrays, a FastClear2DArray stores data in column-major order, meaning that elements with adjacent x locations and identical y locations are stored contiguously in memory. This variant of Fast2DArray uses an extra 4 bytes per element but has O(1) clear times. If this array contains references to reference types, the referenced objects will *not* be garbage-collected after clearing.

member.name: T:Halfling.Physics2D.Collision.ManifoldPoint
member.summary: A manifold point is a contact point belonging to a contact manifold. It holds details related to the geometry and dynamics of the contact points. The local point usage depends on the manifold type: -ShapeType.Circles: the local center of circleB -SeparationFunction.FaceA: the local center of cirlceB or the clip point of polygonB -SeparationFunction.FaceB: the clip point of polygonA This structure is stored across time steps, so we keep it small. Note: the impulses are used for internal caching and may not provide reliable contact forces, especially for high speed collisions.

member.name: T:Halfling.Physics2D.Collision.Manifold
member.summary: A manifold for two touching convex Shapes. Box2D supports multiple types of contact: - Clip point versus plane with radius - Point versus point with radius (circles) The local point usage depends on the manifold type: - ShapeType.Circles: the local center of circleA - SeparationFunction.FaceA: the center of faceA - SeparationFunction.FaceB: the center of faceB Similarly the local normal usage: - ShapeType.Circles: not used - SeparationFunction.FaceA: the normal on polygonA - SeparationFunction.FaceB: the normal on polygonB We store contacts in this way so that position correction can account for movement, which is critical for continuous physics. All contact scenarios must be expressed in one of these types. This structure is stored across time steps, so we keep it small.

member.name: T:Halfling.Physics2D.Collision.DynamicTree`1
member.summary:
A dynamic tree arranges data in a binary tree to accelerate queries such as volume queries and ray casts. Leafs are proxies with an AABB. In the tree we expand the proxy AABB by Settings.b2_fatAABBFactor so that the proxy AABB is bigger than the client object. This allows the client object to move by small amounts without triggering a tree update.
Nodes are pooled and relocatable, so we use node indices rather than pointers.

member.summary: Ray-cast against the proxies in the tree. This relies on the callback to perform a exact ray-cast in the case were the proxy contains a Shape. member.name: T:Halfling.Physics2D.Common.Decomposition.BayazitDecomposer
member.summary:
Convex decomposition algorithm created by Mark Bayazit (http://mnbayazit.com/)
Properties: - Tries to decompose using polygons instead of triangles. - Tends to produce optimal results with low processing time. - Running time is O(nr), n = number of vertices, r = reflex vertices. - Does not support holes.
For more information about this algorithm, see http://mnbayazit.com/406/bayazit

member.name: M:Halfling.Physics2D.Common.Decomposition.BayazitDecomposer.ConvexPartition(Halfling.Physics2D.Common.Vertices)
member.summary: Decompose the polygon into several smaller non-concave polygon. If the polygon is already convex, it will return the original polygon, unless it is over Settings.MaxPolygonVertices.

member.name: T:Halfling.Physics2D.Common.Decomposition.CDTDecomposer
member.summary:
2D constrained Delaunay triangulation algorithm. Based on the paper "Sweep-line algorithm for constrained Delaunay triangulation" by V. Domiter and and B. Zalik
Properties: - Creates triangles with a large interior angle. - Supports holes - Generate a lot of garbage due to incapsulation of the Poly2Tri library. - Running time is O(n^2), n = number of vertices. - Does not care about winding order.
Source: http://code.google.com/p/poly2tri/

Requirements: 1. a,b and c form a triangle. 2. a and d is know to be on opposite side of bc
a + / \ / \ b/ \c +-------+ / B \ / \
Facts: d has to be in area B to have a chance to be inside the circle formed by a,b and c d is outside B if orient2d(a,b,d) or orient2d(c,a,d) is CW This preknowledge gives us a way to optimize the incircle test

member.name: M:Halfling.Physics2D.Common.Decomposition.EarclipDecomposer.TriangulatePolygon(Halfling.Physics2D.Common.Vertices,System.Single)
member.summary:
Triangulates a polygon using simple ear-clipping algorithm. Returns size of Triangle array unless the polygon can't be triangulated. This should only happen if the polygon self-intersects, though it will not _always_ return null for a bad polygon - it is the caller's responsibility to check for self-intersection, and if it doesn't, it should at least check that the return value is non-null before using. You're warned!
Triangles may be degenerate, especially if you have identical points in the input to the algorithm. Check this before you use them.
This is totally unoptimized, so for large polygons it should not be part of the simulation loop.
member.remarks: Only works on simple polygons.

Finds and fixes "pinch points," points where two polygon vertices are at the same point.
If a pinch point is found, pin is broken up into poutA and poutB and true is returned; otherwise, returns false.

member.name: T:Halfling.Physics2D.Common.Decomposition.SeidelDecomposer
member.summary:
Convex decomposition algorithm created by Raimund Seidel
Properties: - Decompose the polygon into trapezoids, then triangulate. - To use the trapezoid data, use ConvexPartitionTrapezoid() - Generate a lot of garbage due to incapsulation of the Poly2Tri library. - Running time is O(n log n), n = number of vertices. - Running time is almost linear for most simple polygons. - Does not care about winding order.
For more information, see Raimund Seidel's paper "A simple and fast incremental randomized algorithm for computing trapezoidal decompositions and for triangulating polygons"
See also: "Computational Geometry", 3rd edition, by Mark de Berg et al, Chapter 6.2 "Computational Geometry in C", 2nd edition, by Joseph O'Rourke
Original code from the Poly2Tri project by Mason Green. http://code.google.com/p/poly2tri/source/browse?repo=archive#hg/scala/src/org/poly2tri/seidel
This implementation is from Dec 14, 2010

member.summary: This method detects if two line segments (or lines) intersect, and, if so, the point of intersection. Use the and parameters to set whether the intersection point must be on the first and second line segments. Setting these both to true means you are doing a line-segment to line-segment intersection. Setting one of them to true means you are doing a line to line-segment intersection test, and so on. Note: If two line segments are coincident, then no intersection is detected (there are actually infinite intersection points). Author: Jeremy Bell
member.param: The first point of the first line segment.
The second point of the first line segment.
The first point of the second line segment.
The second point of the second line segment.
This is set to the intersection point if an intersection is detected.
Set this to true to require that the intersection point be on the first line segment.
Set this to true to require that the intersection point be on the second line segment.
member.returns: True if an intersection is detected, false otherwise.

member.summary:
Implements "A new algorithm for Boolean operations on general polygons" available here: http://liama.ia.ac.cn/wiki/_media/user:dong:dong_cg_05.pdf Merges two polygons, a subject and a clip with the specified operation. Polygons may not be self-intersecting.
Warning: May yield incorrect results or even crash if polygons contain collinear points.
member.param: The subject polygon.
The clip polygon, which is added, substracted or intersected with the subject
The operation to be performed. Either Union, Difference or Intersection.
The error generated (if any)
member.returns: A list of closed polygons, which make up the result of the clipping operation. Outer contours are ordered counter clockwise, holes are ordered clockwise.

member.summary:
Marching squares over the given domain using the mesh defined via the dimensions (wid,hei) to build a set of polygons such that f(x,y) less than 0, using the given number 'bin' for recursive linear inteprolation along cell boundaries.
if 'comb' is true, then the polygons will also be composited into larger possible concave polygons.

Recursive linear interpolation for use in marching squares *
Recursive linear interpolation for use in marching squares *
Square value for use in marching squares *

Look-up table to relate polygon key with the vertices that should be used for the sub polygon in marching squares * Perform a single celled marching square for for the given cell defined by (x0,y0) (x1,y1) using the function f for recursive interpolation, given the look-up table 'fs' of the values of 'f' at cell vertices with the result to be stored in 'poly' given the actual coordinates of 'ax' 'ay' in the marching squares mesh. *
Used in polygon composition to composit polygons into scan lines Combining polya and polyb into one super-polygon stored in polya. *

members.member:
Winding number test for a point in a polygon.
See more info about the algorithm here: http://softsurfer.com/Archive/algorithm_0103/algorithm_0103.htm The point to be tested. -1 if the winding number is zero and the point is outside the polygon, 1 if the point is inside the polygon, and 0 if the point is on the polygons edge.

member.summary: Compute the sum of the angles made between the test point and each pair of points making up the polygon. If this sum is 2pi then the point is an interior point, if 0 then the point is an exterior point. ref: http://ozviz.wasp.uwa.edu.au/~pbourke/geometry/insidepoly/ - Solution 2

member.name: P:Halfling.Physics2D.Dynamics.Body.Enabled
member.summary: Set the active state of the body. An inactive body is not simulated and cannot be collided with or woken up. If you pass a flag of true, all fixtures will be added to the broad-phase. If you pass a flag of false, all fixtures will be removed from the broad-phase and all contacts will be destroyed. Fixtures and joints are otherwise unaffected. You may continue to create/destroy fixtures and joints on inactive bodies. Fixtures on an inactive body are implicitly inactive and will not participate in collisions, ray-casts, or queries. Joints connected to an inactive body are implicitly inactive. An inactive body is still owned by a b2World object and remains in the body list. Warning: This property is readonly during callbacks.
member.value: true if active; otherwise, false.

member.name: T:Halfling.Physics2D.Dynamics.Joints.GearJoint
member.summary:
A gear joint is used to connect two joints together. Either joint can be a revolute or prismatic joint. You specify a gear ratio to bind the motions together: coordinate1 + ratio * coordinate2 = ant The ratio can be negative or positive. If one joint is a revolute joint and the other joint is a prismatic joint, then the ratio will have units of length or units of 1/length.
Warning: You have to manually destroy the gear joint if jointA or jointB is destroyed.

member.name: T:Halfling.Physics2D.Dynamics.Joints.RopeJoint
member.summary:
A rope joint enforces a maximum distance between two points on two bodies. It has no other effect. It can be used on ropes that are made up of several connected bodies, and if there is a need to support a heavy body. This joint is used for stabiliation of heavy objects on soft constraint joints.
Warning: if you attempt to change the maximum length during the simulation you will get some non-physical behavior. Use the DistanceJoint instead if you want to dynamically control the length.

member.name: T:Halfling.Physics2D.Dynamics.Joints.WeldJoint
member.summary:
A weld joint essentially glues two bodies together. A weld joint may distort somewhat because the island constraint solver is approximate.
The joint is soft constraint based, which means the two bodies will move relative to each other, when a force is applied. To combine two bodies in a rigid fashion, combine the fixtures to a single body instead.

member.summary: A wheel joint. This joint provides two degrees of freedom: translation along an axis fixed in bodyA and rotation in the plane. You can use a joint limit to restrict the range of motion and a joint motor to drive the rotation or to model rotational friction. This joint is designed for vehicle suspensions.

Ray-cast the world for all fixtures in the path of the ray. Your callback controls whether you get the closest point, any point, or n-points. The ray-cast ignores shapes that contain the starting point.

member.name: F:Halfling.Physics2D.Settings.AutoClearForces
member.summary: By default, forces are cleared automatically after each call to Step. The default behavior is modified with this setting. The purpose of this setting is to support sub-stepping. Sub-stepping is often used to maintain a fixed sized time step under a variable frame-rate. When you perform sub-stepping you should disable auto clearing of forces and instead call ClearForces after all sub-steps are complete in one pass of your game loop.

member.name: T:Halfling.Scene2D.SceneComponent
member.summary: Base class for behaviors that can be attached to nodes. Contains protected Update, Draw, and Input methods that when overridden trigger the automatic insertion of the object into the SceneRoot's Updateables, BoundedRenderables, and Inputables collections.
member.remarks: Reading the state of the scene graph is always thread safe as long as there are no concurrent modifying threads. Subscribing to and unsubscribing from events is also thread-safe. Some methods are thread-safe as documented.

member.name: T:Halfling.Serialization.ReflectiveSerializationAttribute
member.summary: Controls how the content of objects are serialized and deserialized. If a type doesn't have a SerializeContent attribute, then it may still be serialized and deserialized using reflection, in which case all public fields and properties will be serialized, in addition to any non-public fields and properties with the Serial attribute.

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.ReflectiveSerializationAttribute.Explicit
member.summary: Gets or sets whether or not only those fields and properties marked with a Serialize attribute will be serialized and deserialized. If false, then all public fields and properties will be serialized, in addition to any non-public fields and properties with the Serial attribute. The default is false.

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.ReflectiveSerializationAttribute.InvokeDefaultConstructor
member.summary: Gets or sets whether the default constructor will be invoked to create the object when only content-deserialization is available. If false, then no constructor will be invoked and the type will be completely uninitialized before its contents are deserialized. The default is true.

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.ReflectiveSerializationAttribute.IncludeInterfaces
member.summary: Gets or sets whether interface members should be serialized and deserialized. If null, then parent interface members will only be serialized if the root type is also an interface.

member.name: T:Halfling.Serialization.SerializerSpecificAttribute
member.summary: The base class for attributes that can only be applied to specific serializers.

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.SerializerSpecificAttribute.OnlySerializers
member.summary: Gets or sets the serializer types that this attribute will apply to. If null, this attribute will apply to all serializers except those specified in ExcludeSerializers.

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.SerializerSpecificAttribute.ExcludeSerializers
member.summary: Gets or sets the serializer types that this attribute will not apply to if OnlySerializers is null.

member.name: M:Halfling.Serialization.SerializerSpecificAttribute.AppliesToSerializer(System.Type)
member.summary: Returns whether this attribute applies to a serializer of the specified type.

member.name: T:Halfling.Serialization.SerializeAttribute
member.summary: When attributed to a field or property, allows the serialization and deserialization behavior of that field or property to be customized. If the SerializeContent attribute is defined on a class and the Explicit property is true, then only fields and properties with a Serialize attribute will be serialized and deserialized.

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.SerializeAttribute.Read
member.summary: Set to false to prevent deserialization.

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.SerializeAttribute.Write
member.summary: Set to false to prevent serialization.

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.SerializeAttribute.ReadFlags
member.summary: Gets or sets the ReadFlags used when deserializing the attributed field or property.

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.SerializeAttribute.WriteFlags
member.summary: Gets or sets the WriteFlags used when deserializing the attributed field or property.

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.SerializeAttribute.Optional
member.summary: Gets or sets whether the attributed field or property is optional when deserializing.

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.SerializeAttribute.ReadContentOnly
member.summary: Gets or sets whether, when deserialize the attributed field or property, it is assumed to already exist and only its content will be deserialized instead of creating a whole new instance. The attributed field or property is assumed to be non-null when deserializing.

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.SerializeAttribute.Alias
member.summary: Gets or sets the alias to use when serializing and deserializing the attributed field or property. If null, the name of the attributed property will be used.

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.SerializeAttribute.AlternateAliases
member.summary: Gets or sets the alternate aliases that can be used to deserialize this field if the main alias isn't found.

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.SerializeAttribute.DefaultValue
member.summary: If not null and Optional is true, stores the default value to be placed in the attributed field or property.

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.SerializeAttribute.ProgressWeight
member.summary: Gets or sets the relative progress weight to use when serializing or deserializing the attributed field or property.

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.SerializeAttribute.OverrideSerializer
member.summary: Gets or sets a type of custom serializer to use for the attributed field or property in place of the normal serialization process.

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.SerializeAttribute.OverrideDeserializer
member.summary: Gets or sets a type of custom deserializer to use for the attributed field or property in place of the normal deserialization process.

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.SerializeAttribute.OverrideContentDeserializer
member.summary: Gets or sets a type of custom content deserializer to use for the attributed field or property in place of the normal content deserialization process.

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.SerializeAttribute.InheritMember
member.summary: Gets or sets whether the MemberInfo passed when deserializing the attributed field or property will be the MemberInfo passed when deserializing the containing object, as opposed to the MemberInfo of the attributed field or property itself.

member.name: T:Halfling.Serialization.SerialBaseTypeAttribute
member.summary: Informs the serializer that, when reading or writing the attributed type, additional information should be written about which derived type is actually being serialized or deserialized.

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.SerialBaseTypeAttribute.Explicit
member.summary: If true, derived types must be tagged with the SerialDerivedType attribute in order to be serialized or deserialized.

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.SerialBaseTypeAttribute.TypeFieldName
member.summary: The name of the field to which type information will be read and written. The default is "Type".

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.SerialBaseTypeAttribute.ValueFieldName
member.summary: The name of the field to which the value of the actual derived type will be read and written. The default is "Value".

member.name: T:Halfling.Serialization.SerialDerivedTypeAttribute
member.summary: Informs the serializer that, when reading or writing a type with the SerialBaseType attribute, that the attributed type is a valid derived type to actually serialize or deserialize. This attribute is only required if the SerialBaseType's Explicit property is true.

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.SerialDerivedTypeAttribute.TypeName
member.summary: Gets or sets the string used to uniquely identify the derived type when serializing or deserializing the base type. By default (if null), the derived type's short name (that is, it's name without namespace or assembly qualifications) will be used.

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.SerialDerivedTypeAttribute.GenericTypeArguments
member.summary: Gets or sets the array of types to use as the derived type's generic arguments when serializing or deserializing the base type.

member.name: T:Halfling.Serialization.TrackMultipleReferencesAttribute
member.summary: Informs the serializer that, when serializing, it should only serialize each unique instance of the attributed object once and reference back to the already-serialized object when it is referenced multiple times. When deserializing, the serializer will return the same instance when a reference is read.

member.name: T:Halfling.Serialization.DisableNullSerializationAttribute
member.summary: Informs that serializer that it shouldn't handle null serialization and that the attributed type will handle it itself if necessary.

member.name: T:Halfling.Serialization.ParallelDeserializeAttribute
member.summary: Informs the serializer that, if possible, the attributed collection should be deserialized in parallel.

member.name: P:Halfling.Serialization.ParallelDeserializeAttribute.EnableParallelDeserialization
member.summary: Gets or sets whether parallel deserialization is enabled for fields and properties marked with ParallelDeserializeAttribute. The default is enabled.

member.summary: The game window will be displayed on the desktop but without any titlebar or border. The position and size of the window will exactly match the screen size.

member.summary: The game window will be displayed in exclusive full-screen, occupying the entire screen and possibly using a non-desktop resolution.

member.name: T:Halfling.Windows.VSyncMode
member.summary: Specifies whether and how the application's rendering will be synchronized with the monitor's refresh rate.

member.name: F:Halfling.Windows.VSyncMode.Off
member.summary: Rendering will not be synchornized with the monitor's refresh rate. This provides the least latency and does not limit FPS, but may result in screen tearing and potentially uses more CPU/GPU power.

member.name: F:Halfling.Windows.VSyncMode.OnDoubleBuffered
member.summary: Rendering will be synchronized with the monitor's refresh rate. This limits FPS to the monitor's refresh rate and introduces some latency, but eliminates screen tearing.

member.name: F:Halfling.Windows.VSyncMode.OnTripleBuffered
member.summary: Rendering will be synchronized with the monitor's refresh rate using an additional frame buffer. This limits FPS to the monitor's refresh rate and may add some additional latency on top of double-buffering but may increase and smooth out overall FPS. Triple-buffering uses a small amount of additional video memory.
